analysis: Documentation-only PR. docs/developer/test.md adds a section on SDK 27.2 Date-comparison checks (scripts/test-check-date-comparisons.py, scripts/test-check-provider-weak-imports.py, scripts/check-date-comparisons.py). The supplied excerpts at head lines 2297-3209 are existing test-procedure prose; the only changed range is head 1059-1072, which is not among the supplied text units, but its patch excerpt is complete and I examined it. docs/operations/provider-release.md (patch, hunk @@ -629 / head 632-636) adds a release-lane step: scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py runs on every built binary before handoff and refuses binaries importing back-deployed Date.>= or Date.<=, which crash on pre-release macOS 27.2. This is a new release-integrity control and an availability aid. It touches no runtime code, keys, coordinator protocol, attestation, encryption, or the prefix cache (T-041), so it opens no new attack surface. Remaining unverified contracts: the scripts themselves, their CI wiring, and the build guide anchor (build.md#sdk-27-release-builds-and-caches) are not in the supplied evidence, so the doc's claim that the release lane enforces the check cannot be confirmed. This is a documentation-accuracy question, not a security regression. The threat model does not need an update for this change. No findings.
